title: Maps to a constant group scheme are clopen decompositions
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an abelian group, and let $T_E:=\coprod_{e\in E}T$ be the constant group scheme over $T$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. For every object $U\to T$ of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], giving a $T$-morphism $U\to T_E$ is equivalent to giving a family of pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subschemes $(U_e\subseteq U)_{e\in E}$ whose union is $U$ (only finitely many are nonempty when $U$ is quasi-compact). Equivalently it is a map $|U|\to E$ whose fibres are open and closed. Under this equivalence, the canonical map $E\to h_{T_E}(U)=\operatorname{Mor}_T(U,T_E)$ sends $e$ to the morphism with $U_e=U$ and $U_{e'}=\varnothing$ for $e'\ne e$, hence to the constant map with value $e$; the group law is pointwise addition.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5), using Groupoids, Example 39.5.6 (Tag 03YW) for the constant group scheme and its decomposition into copies of the base

mathlib_searches.query: a morphism to the constant group scheme coproduct of copies of the base is a clopen decomposition
mathlib_searches.results: No scheme-theoretic theorem identifying maps to an arbitrary coproduct of copies of the base with clopen-valued maps; only generic coproduct and locally constant APIs

mathlib_searches.query: scheme morphism into disjoint union iff open and closed inverse-image pieces
mathlib_searches.results: No direct constant-group-scheme/clopen decomposition declaration; `Topology.LocallyConstant` gives the topological analogue but not the scheme representability statement

mathlib_searches.results: No theorem matching the stated scheme morphism/decomposition equivalence
